Reflection note - Specimen s_e212dc8248 (ALLN) - correct prediction:

**Outcome:** Predicted Protein degradation p=0.58; BBBC021 annotation = Protein degradation; code score correct.

**Evidence that supported this:**
- NSC vote 3/4 wells Protein degradation (e7). High similarity at active doses: 30uM similarity 0.692 and 10uM similarity 0.757 to Protein degradation reference (MG-132 3.0uM similarity 0.655 top neighbor), dose-dependent.
- Strong dose phenotypes: tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (e8) up to z=+42.5 at 30uM (e2), nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 (e9) down to z=-25.3, frac_multinucleate_proxy +7.4 at 10uM (e4), cell_count loss rho -0.80, cell solidity/form_factor loss. Microscopist confirmed sparse fields, irregular lobed nuclei, spiky cells, retained but heterogeneous tubulin + bright variable actin (e6, e17) - compatible with cytokinesis failure.
- 10uM microscopist call "Aurora kinase inhibitors" (e17) due to multinucleation illustrates overlap: proteasome inhibition blocks cyclin/Securin degradation -> mitotic exit/cytokinesis failure -> secondary polyploidy/multinucleation mimicking Aurora inhibition. I kept Aurora as 0.22 alternative on board (e18) but did not override NSC because signal consistent across 2 independent high doses and k-neighbours included microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers with lower mean similarity.

**Identity check:** lookup_compound ALLN -> PubChem mismatch noted: name ALLN = CID 6915732 D-Allosamine vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339 (2S)-2-acetamido-4-methyl-N-[(2S)-4-methyl-1-oxo-1-(1-oxohexan-2-ylamino)pentan-2-yl]pentanamide (calpain inhibitor I / N-acetyl-Leu-Leu-Norleucinal). ChEMBL: no curated mechanism (e21) - expected for tool compound.

Literature: PMID 35716322 shows ALLN acts via inhibition of noncaspase proteases calpain and proteasome, modulating degradation of pro-/anti-apoptotic proteins and inducing apoptosis, consistent with Protein degradation MoA class assignment. PMID 10597248 illustrates precedent for regulation of k

reflection.text:
Unblinded as ALLN - verdict correct: Protein degradation with p=0.58, Truth=Protein degradation. The call was correct but at modest confidence, which matches the evidence.

What got it right: The quantitative texture/nuclear morphology was decisive and dose-dependent. Wells w_6824fff027 (30 uM, e2) and w_daa103d348 (10 uM, e4) both showed extreme tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.5 / +21.9 and nuc_solidity z=-25.3 / -23.7 with actin changes, while w_799403842a (1 uM, e3) was largely baseline. Dose_response confirmed this was not a single-dose artifact: tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 (e8), nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 p=0 (e9), cell_eccentricity rho=+1.00 p=0 (e16), with supportive trends for frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 (e10), frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 (e15) and cell_count rho=-0.80 (e11). That pattern - tubulin bundling/Texture increase + solidity loss + multinucleation/broad shape change + density loss - is not specific by itself, but compare_to_reference_atlas over the 4 acquired wells (e7) gave NSC 3/4 Protein degradation with high similarity 0.76 at 10 uM and 0.69 at 30 uM, vs k-neighbour split 3/10 DNA replication, 2/10 Protein degradation. I weighted the NSC vote because it uses the full profile at the active doses.

What misled / what I missed: describe_phenotype was unstable: e6 (2 fields, high dose) = unknown, e17 (same method at 10 uM) = Aurora kinase inhibitors. In the hypothesis update (e18) I kept Aurora 0.22 for that reason, citing e4/e10/e15/e17 as support, with Microtubule stabilizers 0.07 also driven only by e2/e4/e8. In retrospect both alternatives were texture-driven mimics: Aurora inhibitors also produce multinucleation and low density, but e13 nuc_area rho=+0.00 p=1 and the inconsistent microscopy across doses contradicted a true polyploidy/Aurora phenotype. I should have down-weighted a single-dose microscopist call vs the 2-dose NSC consensus.

Acquisition choices: Starting at dose 6 (30 uM) was efficient to see a strong phenotype with n=103 cells, then bracketing with 1 uM (e3, n=186), 10 uM (e4, n=95) and 0.3 uM (e5, n=256, essentially null with eccentricity -2.9) established dose-dependency, but sampling only 4/8 doses via list_available_experiments (e1) left no data at 100 uM or 0.03-0.1 uM to define EC50 or toxicity plateau; all inferences rely on n=1 per dose, so p-values in e10/e11/e15 are underpowered (p=0.2, n.s.).

Unblinding check: lookup_compound (e20/e21) returned CID 6915732 for ALLN with no curated ChEMBL mechanism and flagged a structure mismatch to BBBC021 CID 21118339, but name and functional literature align. Search return e22 (28 hits) included the expected mechanism: inhibition of noncaspase proteases calpain and proteasome via ALLN and Bortezomib PMID 35716322, which supports Protein degradation as the correct umbrella MoA despite ALLN being primarily described as a calpain/proteasome inhibitor, not a highly selective proteasome inhibitor. I did not have a functional assay in-run to separate proteasome vs calpain (e23 returned 0 hits), so submitting Protein degradation without that orthogonal ubiquitin/p21/MCL1 or chymotrypsin-like activity data was appropriate for this screening tool.
